Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that claims 1-46 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103 for at least the reasons set forth below. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.
Claims 1, 16 and 32

Without conceding the correctness of the rejections in the Office Action, the claims have been amended to change "first position" to "first rotor position" and "second position" to "second rotor position." These amendments clarify that the position of the rotor, which is part of the rotor assembly or a pylon, is changed. Support for the amendments can be found in paragraphs [0030]- [0031] and FIGS. 1A-2B.

The Office Action equated "moving the rotor assembly or a pylon thereof from a first position ... to a second position" previously recited in claims 1, 16 and 32 to the "particular positions of the power control lever 30" of Fisher. (pages 4 and 29-30). Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the different positions of the Fisher's power control level 30 change the speed/thrust of the rotor, but they do not change the position of the rotor. (paragraphs [0024], [0028], [0030], [0053]-[0054], Figs. 6-9). As a result, Fisher's "particular positions of the power control lever 30" are not equivalent to "moving the rotor assembly or a pylon thereof from a first rotor position ... to a second rotor position" as recited in claims 1, 16 and 32, as amended.

The Office Action stated that "Fisher et al. does not appear to explicitly disclose "automatically changing a rotor speed of the rotor assembly", but Barnes discloses this feature. (page 3). Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Barnes only discloses automatically changing rotor speeds from a high-speed to a low-speed. (paragraph [0017]). As a result, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Fisher and Barnes do not disclose, teach or suggest "automatically changing a rotor speed of the rotor assembly of the tiltrotor aircraft while moving the rotor assembly or a pylon thereof from a first rotor position and a first rotor speed to a second rotor position and a second rotor speed over a time period in accordance with an acceleration-rate profile
that varies over the time period" as recited in claim 1. (emphasis added). Claims 16 and 32 recite similar elements.

Notably, the Office Action did not equate the first position and the second position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof as previously recited in claims 4, 20 and 36 to the different positions of the Fisher's power control level 30. (pages 8-9). Instead, the Office Action cited Elfeky, which discloses a two rotor air vehicle in which the two rotors can be tilted using a servo mechanism. (Abstract). Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Elfeky does not cure the deficiencies of Fisher or Barnes because Elfeky does not disclose, teach or suggest "automatically ... moving the rotor assembly or a pylon thereof from a first rotor position ... to a second rotor position ... over a time period in accordance with an acceleration-rate profile that varies over the time period" as recited in claim 1. (emphasis added). Claims 16 and 32 recite similar elements.
In addition, the Office Action stated that Fisher discloses a tiltrotor aircraft. (page 2). The Office Action also stated that the use of "tiltrotor aircraft" in the claims was an "intended use of

the claimed invention." (page 28). Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the term "tiltrotor aircraft" is in the body of the claims and provides a structural limitation that must be considered. A "rotor assembly of the tiltrotor aircraft" is structurally different from the rotor assembly of a helicopter or regular aircraft because the rotor assembly in a tiltrotor aircraft is capable of rotating in multiple positions relative to the fuselage; whereas, the rotor assembly of a helicopter or regular aircraft rotates in a single position relative to the fuselage. As a result, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Fisher's use of the term "aircraft or airplane" (paragraph [0017]) does not disclose, teach or suggest a "tiltrotor aircraft" as recited in claims 1, 16 and 32. Likewise, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Barnes discloses a helicopter (Abstract), which does not disclose, teach or suggest a "tiltrotor aircraft" as recited in claims 1, 16 and 32.

For at least the foregoing reasons, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Fisher and Barnes, either alone or in combination, do not disclose, teach or suggest each and every element of claims 1, 16 and 32. Claims 1, 16 and 32 are, therefore, allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the deficiencies detailed above in reference to the cited references are sufficient to traverse the rejections. As a result, any additional distinctions between the claims and the cited references are unnecessary and applicant(s) reserve(s) the right to present additional arguments against the statements and characterizations stated in the Office Action, and the cited reference in the event the rejections are not withdrawn.
Claims 2-3, 19 and 35

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that claims 2-3, 19 and 35 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103 because they directly or indirectly depend from claims 1, 16 and 32, which are allowable for at least the reasons set forth above. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

The Office Action equated "the first position" and "the second position" previously recited in claims 2-3, 19 and 35 to the positions of the power control lever 30 of Fisher. (pages 5 and 29- 30). Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the different positions of the Fisher's power control level 30 change the speed/thrust of the rotor, but they do not change the position of the rotor. (paragraphs [0024], [0028], [0030], [0053]-[0054], Figs. 6-9). As a result, Fisher's particular positions of the power control lever 30 are not equivalent to "the first rotor position" and "the second rotor position" as recited in claims 2-3, 19 and 35, as amended.

For at least the foregoing reasons, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Fisher and Barnes, either alone or in combination, do not disclose, teach or suggest each and every element of claims 2-3, 19 and 35. Claims 2-3, 19 and 35 are, therefore, allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

between the claims and the cited references are unnecessary and applicant(s) reserve(s) the right to present additional arguments against the statements and characterizations stated in the Office Action, and the cited reference in the event the rejections are not withdrawn.
Claims 4, 20 and 36

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that claims 4, 20 and 36 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103 because they directly or indirectly depend from claims 1, 16 and 32, which are allowable for at least the reasons set forth above. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Elfeky discloses a two rotor air vehicle in which the two rotors can be tilted using a servo mechanism. (Abstract). Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Elfeky does not disclose, teach or suggest "automatically ... moving the rotor assembly or a pylon thereof from a first rotor position ... to a second rotor position ... over a time period in accordance with an acceleration-rate profile that varies over the time period" as recited in claim 1 (emphasis added), wherein "the first rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof is generally parallel to a yaw axis of the tiltrotor aircraft, and the second rotor position of the rotor assembly or pylon thereof is generally parallel to a roll axis of the tiltrotor aircraft; or the first rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof is generally parallel to the roll axis of the tiltrotor aircraft, and the second rotor position of the rotor assembly or the pylon thereof is generally parallel to the yaw axis of the tiltrotor aircraft" as recited in claim 4. The combination of claims 16 and 30, and 32 and 36 recite similar elements.

For at least the foregoing reasons, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Fisher, Barnes and Elfeky, either alone or in combination, do not disclose, teach or suggest each and every element of claims 2-3, 19 and 35. Claims 2-3, 19 and 35 are, therefore, allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

The Office Action rejected claims 1-46 on the grounds of nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-30 of U.S. Patent No. 11,072,434.

The terminal disclaimer was approved on February 20, 2025. Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that claims 1-46 are allowable. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

For the reasons set forth above, Applicant(s) respectfully request(s) reconsideration by the examiner and withdrawal of the rejections. Applicant(s) submit(s) that claims 1-46 are fully patentable.
